title: staged-activation-controller-for-optimize-autopilot
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers using Redwood Optimize want automated recommendations (batching/cache/quantization) to be applied with minimal manual intervention, but teams need strong safety controls to avoid regressions in latency, cost, or quality. Current MVP auto-apply prototype risks wide impact if a bad config is promoted too quickly; there is no staged activation controller that enforces progressive exposure, verifies metrics, and escalates to human approvals when thresholds are exceeded.

Goal: Build a Staged Activation Controller (SAC) that orchestrates progressive enabling of Optimize suggestions across traffic segments and enforces canary validation policies, automated rollback hooks, and human-in-the-loop approvals for risky changes. The SAC sits between Optimize recommendations and the runtime config applier and integrates with Console for visibility and manual overrides.

Scope:
- Controller that executes a staged activation plan: dry-run -> canary (1% traffic) -> ramp (5/25/50) -> full.
- Pluggable validation checks executed at each stage: latency SLO, token cost delta, result-quality regression (via eval hooks), error-rate thresholds.
- Automated rollback when validation fails, with visibility and safe fallback to previous quant/profile.
- Human approval gating for changes flagged as high-risk (e.g., model quantization, new kernel selection, or cost delta > 15%).
- Console UX: per-recommendation timeline view, stage status, reason for rollback, and a one-click revert.
- API changes: POST /optimize/activations to create staged plans; webhook callbacks for stage events.
- Telemetry and alerting: per-stage metrics exported to observability stack and a default Grafana dashboard.

Non-goals: Full A/B traffic splitting (beyond simple percentage routing), automated model re-training, policy-based offense detection (this ticket provides the hooks for later).
acceptance_criteria: Controller can create and execute staged activation plans via API and Console
Canary stage routes live traffic (configurable percent) and collects real-time metrics for validation
Validation rules are configurable and include latency SLO, token-cost delta, and error-rate thresholds
Automated rollback is triggered within 5 minutes of a failed validation and restores previous configuration reliably
High-risk changes require explicit approver consent in Console before moving past canary stage
Console shows timeline, stage-level metrics, and one-click revert for any activation
End-to-end tests and integration tests exist for the happy path, failure + rollback, and approval flow
Documentation and runbook for on-call engineers describing failure modes and manual rollback steps
